title: Quiet-degradation sweep and sample-capture: GPU node instability hypothesis log
content:
Summary:

This is a working notes + mini-runbook for the "quiet degradation" pattern we've observed on a small population of GPU nodes across the west-2 cluster. Unlike loud panics or immediate kernel crashes, these nodes show gradual increases in request latency and occasional partial failures after 12-72 hours under sustained long-sequence chat workloads. Early signals: slow rise in soft ECC correctable error counters, intermittent nvlink retransmit spikes, and increasing frequency of CUDA context timeouts (sometimes recovered by container restart).

Why this doc exists:
- Capture reproducible sampling plan for collecting traces and kernel logs with minimal customer impact.
- Record hypotheses and lightweight experiments to validate root causes (thermal vs fabric vs driver state drift vs memory slab corruption).
- Draft an operator checklist for on-call to capture a node and rotate traffic safely.

Observed signals (pattern):
- Token-level p50/p95 latency gradually increases ~10-25% over ~24–48h for a pinned model route.
- Prometheus metric gpu_ecc_correctable_total shows a sheen upward correlated to latency rise on the same host (not fleet-wide).
- nvlink_retransmits and nvlink_error_count show sharp short-duration spikes preceding a short window of elevated CUDA errors in application logs.
- dmesg occasionally shows "gpu: GPU X: correctable error" messages, usually not accompanied by hard driver oops or panic.
- Repro rate low in stress tests; appears workload dependent (long sequences, KV cache heavy).

Immediate on-call capture checklist (minimizes impact):
1) Isolate node from new allocations (set node unsched or pause autoscaler allocation).
   - k8s: kubectl cordon <node> && drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
2) Snapshot live telemetry before disruptive ops:
   - curl -s "http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/query?query=gpu_ecc_correctable_total{instance=\"NODE_HOSTNAME\"}"
   - Run nvidia-smi dmon for 60s: 
     nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 1 -c 60 > /var/tmp/nvidia-dmon-$(hostname)-$(date +%s).log
3) Capture kernel log and driver stack traces (rotate to persistent file):
   - journalctl -k -n 500 > /var/tmp/kernel-$(hostname)-$(date +%s).log
   - dmesg -T | tail -n 200 > /var/tmp/dmesg-tail.log
4) Collect NVLink and PCI lane state: 
   - lspci -vvv | grep -A 20 NVIDIA
   - nvidia-smi nvlink --query-gpu=linkState,linkErrorCount --format=csv > /var/tmp/nvlink-state.log
5) Capture driver and container core dump config (if enabled):
   - Check /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern and /sys/module/nvidia/parameters/* for crash capture settings.
6) If safe window, perform a non-disruptive soft reset attempt per our driver safe-reset doc:
   - systemctl stop kubelet && rmmod nvidia_uvm;nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i <gpu_id> (only in maintenance window and with SRE lead approval)

Telemetry queries to run (examples):
- PromQL: increase(gpu_ecc_correctable_total[6h]) BY (instance, gpu)
- PromQL: max_over_time(nvlink_retransmit_count[1h]) by (instance)
- LogQL (Loki): {job="gpu-logs", host="NODE_HOSTNAME"} |~ "correctable error|nvlink|gpu reset|CUDA_ERROR" | line_format "{{.Time}} {{.Message}}"

Hypotheses and small experiments (ordered cheap->expensive):
A) NVLink fabric negotiation/framing drift under sustained KV-cache pressure -> retransmit bursts -> transient stalls.
   - Experiment: schedule pairs of synthetic long-seq runs pinned to GPUs on a suspect host and monitor nvlink_retransmit_count in real time. Run two 6h tasks each with 20 concurrent streams. Compare to control host.
B) Soft ECC accumulation combined with long-running CUDA contexts causes occasional micro-reboots of certain firmware components.
   - Experiment: enable aggressive ECC scrubbing (if supported) on one node and observe whether latency drift rate changes. Capture scrubbing activity logs.
C) Driver memory allocator fragmentation (slab) leading to increasing host-visible latency as allocation/GC overhead grows.
   - Experiment: start a scheduled daily container restart (12h cadence) on small canary pool to see if drift disappears. If yes, points at allocator drift.

Data capture / flight recorder design (proposed):
- Attach a lightweight periodic "flight recorder" to suspect nodes that writes 30s stacked snapshots every 10 minutes for 48h:
  - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,temperature.gpu,memory.used --format=csv -l 30 -f /var/tmp/flight-$(hostname).csv
  - NVLink jitter counter snapshot: run nvlink query at start and end of each 10m window and compute delta.
- Save one contiguous tarball and upload to S3 with tags (node, start_ts, route) for offline correlation.

Runbook draft for low-severity slow-degrade node (for engineers on-call):
1) Mark node unsched and trigger flight recorder capture.
2) If ECC correctables > threshold (e.g., 200 increase in 24h) and nvlink retransmits spike(s) > 10 in 1h: escalate to GPU SRE lead and quiesce node for lab repro.
3) If kernel oops or panic appears: treat as high severity and follow full panic runbook (collect kdump, upload crashcore, schedule immediate repro).
4) If no clear telemetry but latency persists: schedule controlled pod restarts and observe recovery pattern; keep a 24h window for post-mortem.

Safe reproduction recipe (lab):
- Use workload: long-context summarization + streaming KV cache (model: open-gptx-13B sim).
- Sequence lengths: 4k tokens with repeated incremental prefix access to exercise KV cache.
- Run for 48–72h on single node with 8 concurrent streams at target token/sec to mimic production throughput.
- Instrument with perf, nvidia-cupti traces and periodic nvlink snapshots (see flight recorder).

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Is the trend strictly per-hardware revision (we have mixed GA3/E3 boards) or per-driver+firmware versions? Need stable mapping of firmware versions to node IDs (ENG-9876 task).
- Are there correlations with host power delivery/PMIC telemetry? We don't currently pull fine-grained PD telemetry into Prom.
- What is safe threshold for ECC correctables to auto-quarantine a node? Need historical baseline analysis across fleet.

Next actions (short):
- Alejandro: wire a quick Prom dashboard showing 24/48/72h delta for gpu_ecc_correctable_total grouped by hardware SKU (due 2029-03-18).
- Priya: prototype flight-recorder systemd unit and S3 uploader; push minimal collector into telemetry repo PR/432 for review.
- Samir: prepare a lab repro job definition and validate synthetic workload container image; run first 48h job on lab rack and report.

Notes to on-call: this is intentionally a low-noise capture plan. The goal is to observe and correlate before initiating destructive recovery steps. If you need immediate rollback to preserve SLAs, prefer traffic migration/cordon -> ephemeral replacement in dedicated pool.

Appendix: useful commands (copy/paste)
- quick ECC check: for g in $(nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index --format=csv,noheader); do nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.used,utilization.gpu,driver_model.current,serial --format=csv -i $g; done
- nvlink state: nvidia-smi nvlink --query-link=linkState,linkBandwidth,linkErrorCount --format=csv -i 0
- kernel logs: sudo journalctl -k --since "1 hour ago" | tail -n 200

If this document helps with a capture or a postmortem, add notes below the action items and link Incident or Postmortem doc IDs.

-- Maya
